content.text:
I made three fixes to `0.html`. On normal screens it looks the same as before: a 400px black circle in the middle of the page.

- **The circle got cut off on small screens.** It was always 400px wide, so on a smaller screen the centering pushed it past both edges. The part past the left or top edge couldn't be scrolled back into view. This affected phones narrower than 400px (many are 360–393px) and phones turned sideways. The size is now `min(400px, 100dvmin)`, so it shrinks to fit on smaller screens.
- **The page could be bigger than the window.** `width: 100vw` includes the scrollbar's width, so it could add a sideways scrollbar. On phones, `height: 100vh` is taller than what you can see while the browser toolbar is showing, so the page scrolled a little and the circle sat off-center. I removed the width, since the body is already full width, and changed the height to `min-height: 100dvh`.
- **Screen readers had no name for the circle.** I added `role="img" aria-label="Black circle"` to the SVG.

I didn't change the `ae683f770` title or id, since other things may refer to them.

I haven't tested this in a browser. Finding a browser to take screenshots needed approval, which this session can't give. To check it yourself, open the file and make the window narrower or shorter than 400px, or use the phone view in your browser's dev tools.

If by "improve" you meant changing how it looks, tell me what you want.
